subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should deterministic cron outcome verification be a first-class core job contract, or a generic fail-capable plugin hook that can request scheduler-owned retry and escalation?
rationale: Both approaches require new public semantics and security boundaries, and source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers want permanent per-job verifier configuration in core or a reusable plugin extension point.

options.title: Generic verifier contract
options.body: Add a narrow scheduler-owned verifier abstraction with a bounded command implementation and a plugin-capable extension seam, keeping retry, state, and escalation semantics canonical.

options.title: Core postconditions field
options.body: Adopt the proposed per-job postconditions surface directly in cron and own its command security, protocol, UI, migration, and retry behavior in core.

options.title: Plugin hook only
options.body: Add only a fail-capable post-run plugin hook and require external plugins to provide verifier configuration and execution.

recommendation.title: Generic verifier contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow scheduler-owned verifier abstraction with a bounded command implementation and a plugin-capable extension seam, keeping retry, state, and escalation semantics canonical.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing discussion and recent cron runtime, schema, and documentation history make this person the best available owner for the product-boundary decision.
